articles.title: The Growing Debate and Safety Risks of Compounded GLP-1s for Employers
articles.summary: As brand-name GLP-1 shortages fluctuate, employers face mounting pressure regarding employee access to lower-cost compounded alternatives. The controversy highlights significant safety, quality, and legal concerns that self-funded health plans must weigh when designing obesity benefit strategies.
articles.source_line: Source: BioPharma Dive; Wed, 18 Nov 2026 18:52:19 GMT

articles.title: Maryland Becomes First State to Set Price Cap on Ozempic
articles.summary: Maryland has established a state-mandated price cap on Ozempic, marking a major regulatory milestone in the ongoing battle over GLP-1 affordability. This policy precedent could spark similar state-level price interventions nationwide, significantly altering cost projections and formulary management strategies for self-funded employer health plans covering anti-obesity and diabetes medications.

articles.title: Deloitte to Drop GLP-1 Coverage for Weight Loss in 2027
articles.summary: Professional services giant Deloitte announced it will eliminate weight-loss coverage for GLP-1 medications starting in 2027 due to unsustainable cost pressures. This high-profile decision by a major employer signals a potential shifting tide among self-funded plan sponsors grappling with escalating obesity drug spend. It highlights the growing tension between employee benefit expectations and the financial reality of managing specialty drug trends.

articles.title: Scrutinizing PBM Contracts: Key Insights for Plan Sponsors
articles.summary: This Q&A explores strategies for plan sponsors to critically examine PBM contracts, focusing on hidden costs and pricing transparency. It provides actionable guidance for self-funded employers seeking to optimize their pharmacy benefit agreements.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:39:38 GMT

articles.title: Senate Judiciary Committee Advances Legislation Targeting PBM Transparency and Drug Pricing Practices
articles.summary: Witnesses at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing urged lawmakers to pass Grassley-backed bills aimed at increasing transparency and accountability for pharmacy benefit managers. The push for federal reform directly impacts self-funded employers by potentially altering how PBM contracts, rebates, and spread pricing are regulated. This legislative momentum signals continued bipartisan scrutiny on PBM business models and cost structures.

articles.title: CVS Study Finds GLP-1s Offset Costs at $350 Net Price
articles.summary: A new CVS Health study suggests that anti-obesity GLP-1 medications can generate net healthcare savings for payers if the net price drops to $350 or lower per month. This threshold provides a critical benchmark for self-funded employers grappling with whether to cover weight-loss drugs. The finding emphasizes the urgent need for aggressive PBM rebate negotiations and alternative pricing models to make GLP-1 coverage financially viable for employers.

articles.title: CVS Pharmacy Pricing Shakeup Sparks Industry Scrutiny Over Consumer Savings
articles.summary: CVS is planning a major restructuring of its retail pharmacy pricing and operations. For self-funded employers and PBMs, retail pharmacy model shifts directly impact commercial drug spend, consumer out-of-pocket costs, and network dynamics.
articles.source_line: Source: KLAS 8 News Now; Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:41:46 GMT

articles.title: Optum Rx Introduces Digital Tools for Price Transparency and Medication Access
articles.summary: Optum Rx has launched new pharmacy technology solutions aimed at enhancing price transparency and improving medication access for plan members. The initiative reflects growing market pressure on major PBMs to deliver clearer pricing models and better digital tools to employer clients. This development underscores how transparency demands are shaping product roadmaps across the PBM industry.
articles.source_line: Source: Digital Health News; Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:35:00 GMT
